It is very rare in my life that I encounter a woman wearing a Hijab or Burka. Not saying anything about the frequency... only mentioning it because when I do encounter this is is something that I notice. Yesterday I encountered a mother and daughter both wearing hijab and I had the opportunity to be very aware of my own emotions on the subject.

The mother was dressed fairly traditionally... long sleeves, opaque leggings, long tunic style dress and a Hijab. The daughter appeared to be in her early teenage years and was dressed in shorts, a t-shirt and a hijab... but underneath the shorts and t-shirt she was wearing some form of cover-up garment. It looked like she put on a burkini and then put on normal teenager outfit, and then put on a Hijab.

It was hot out but the mother look reasonably comfortable. Her traditional clothes were designed to be worn in warm climates even though they covered her up. The daughter looked miserable. She was sweating profusely because she was basically wearing long-johns in the summer. It was clear that she wanted to dress like a normal teenager and this was the best compromise she could strike with her parents. We were in a public place (super market) and I interacted with them the same way I would interact with any other stranger in the store... a polite smile and nod as we pass in each other in the aisle. The mother acted like I did not exist. The daughter looked at me like a normal teenager... But when we made eye contact she had look of fear come over her face. She dropped her eyes to the ground and took on the most submissive posture you could imagine.

I was overcome with pity and sadness for the daughter, anger towards her father and disgust that the mother would let it happen. How do we let this happen to little girls in modern civilized society? When I see a grown woman dressed like this I generally have much more subdued emotions. I still feel sad; I still feel pity... but when it is an adult I have a thought of "Well, she is an adult and this is a free country. Its her choice." But when I saw this girl I realized that she is not an adult and it is not her choice. Someone forced her dress like that. The libertarian in me says that a parent has the right to raise their children in their own way... but the human being in me said "Fuck this. This is NOT right."

Thanks for letting me vent.
